answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can anchor identities to hydrodynamic telemetry from coastal sensor arrays. Each agent proves uniqueness by executing an attestation kernel that correlates micro-turbulence data recorded at an estuary inlet. An attacker must deploy discrete submerged sensors per identity, incurring recurring hardware and marine maintenance costs. However, slack water at each tide creates laminar flow that degrades entropy, causing temporary verification blackouts.
